Vena exportans sanguinem ex Epate quę scilicet excipit sanguinem & deinceps in membra per ramos & partes distribuit & diffundit, dicitur Vena cava.

Vena cava est Venarum maxima & quasi truncus, sanguinem confectum & beneficio vesiculæ fellis & lienis duplici humore expurgatum, ductu suo per multiplices propagines in universum corpus distribuens.Vena ca-va.
Vena cavæ propagines serie quadam cum supra jecur ascendunt, tum infra ipsum descendunt, partibus comeatum advehentes, quæ omnes non possunt distributionum vinculo colligari.

main_text.p: ADhuc fuerunt organa concoctionis mediatæ: Organa concoctionis immediatè nutritioni infervientes sunt venæ Capillares seu extremitates venularum in singulis alendis membris, in quibus purior sanguinis portio, antecedenteVena Capillares. ante-

page.notes: The initial "A" of "ADhuc" is a large woodcut-style initial, joined to its word as printed. The chyl» mark is doubtful; it may be a printed abbreviation sign for chylus. The page number reads as 295 but the digits are worn. The right margin notes are "Vena ca-va." and "Vena Ca-pillares." with their printed hyphens. Faint show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page are not transcribed.
